On The 5 th Of January, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 34133 of 2025
 Devendra Lodhi
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Pushpendra Dubey - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Sumit Raghuwanshi - Government Advocate for the r
 Order

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No.1224/2023, registered at Police Station - Panagar, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for commission of offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 182, 211, 294,
506, 34 of IPC.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant has relied upon the order dated 12.12.2025 passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No.5429- 5430/2025 and has submitted that the applicant who has not been named in the FIR has played similar role and, therefore, his case may be considered.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has submitted that the applicant a is habitual offender and is involved in one more offence.
Against which counsel for the applicant has submitted that in that case the applicant is acquitted.

Learned counsel for the State has drawn my attention to the earlier order dated 22.01.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.55522/2024 which reads as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:53 2 MCRC-34133-2025 "As prayed by learned counsel for the applicant, this first anticipatory bail application under Section 482 of BNSS filed on behalf of the applicant-Devendra Lodhi is dismissed as withdrawn.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it is directed that if applicant surrenders before the trial Court and moves a bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, the same be decided expeditiously."

5. Considering the same and considering the fact that the applicant is evading his arrest since 2024 and though the first bail application is rejected with a specific direction that if applicant surrenders before the trial Court and moves a bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, the same be decided expeditiously.
Without availing that remedy, successive anticipatory bail application is filed.

Without discussing anything on merit, considering the role of the present applicant and also considering that his first anticipatory bail application is rejected with liberty, which is not availed and neither that order is challenged before the Hon'ble Apex Court, I am of the opinion that consideration of this application amounts to due advantage to the applicant.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT) JUDGE b Devendra Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142429740/
